coverageSpotVerification.detail: Every one of the 58 suite-required assertion -> test mappings in coverage-manifest.json was sampled: each mapped file (scripts/acceptance-m1.mjs, -m2, -m3, -m4, -m5, -m6, -m8 and the shared scripts/suite.mjs) was read in full and each mapping checked against its assertion's observable. Cross-checked against assertions.json, the manifest covers every suite-required assertion of every attempted milestone with no extras (M1 7/7, M2 22/22, M3 7/7, M4 5/5, M5 6/6, M6 5/5, M8 6/6; M7's six are absent, consistent with not-run). No mapping points at a test that fails to exercise its assertion, so no milestone is adjudicated capability-failure. Independently, the grader re-executed all 58 by a different mechanism (custom-client API, direct asset fetches, browser automation, read-only store SQL) and reached the same pass verdict on every one - zero divergence between suiteResult and the grader's independent result anywhere in this report. Four mappings are weaker than ideal and are recorded for transparency, each closed by the grader's own check: m2-a13 proxies 'no preview card' as iframe count 0 (grader verified iframes 0 AND images 0 and the absence of any unfurl code path); m2-a24 checks duplicates but not gaps (grader added a full 16-page cursor walk with monotone .at ordering); m4-a03 registers the video assertion without asserting the media attached (grader asserted type:video, duration 5000 ms and a 49779-byte recipient fetch); m3-a11 asserts only isVisible() for the quoted-reply jump (grader re-ran with 25 filler messages and measured viewport geometry, y 1670 -> 503). One mapping is stronger than required: m8-a01 computes its six expected totals from read-only store SQL and compares them against both the insights query and the six rendered totals.

defects.summary: At the scale envelope the trending query answers complete:false with cut:null, and the Trending screen never surfaces it: src/Social.tsx:321-335 branches only on r.data.length, rendering rows as exhaustive or the <TrendingEmpty/> 'no results' state, while the lane's paged surfaces do render 'Results may be incomplete' (src/Social.tsx:40-42). The platform's client contract says that for complete:false with cut:null a client must render 'Results may be incomplete', even when empty, and never 'no matches'. The ranking itself is correct - the grader matched the API's top-5 against read-only SQL ground truth over 48270 in-window top-level posts, exactly and in order - so this is a correctness-honesty and empty-state defect, not wrong data.

defects.summary: An expired disappearing message can still be rendered at the instant a relaunched client opens the conversation, intermittently under load. The grader's first independent run of the frozen M5 choreography segment failed disappearing-message-expiry-and-purge with 'expired message remained visible after both clients relaunched' after the harness's 300 s wait against a 180 s TTL; the second run of the same segment passed, and a faithful instrumented reproduction passed at every step (control applied, server TTL exactly 180000 ms, server point query null, 0 matching bubbles on both clients at +4 s and +20 s). Tally: 1 failure in 3 grader-driven harness attempts, the failing one while 1-minute load climbed past 37. Not a configuration or server fault and not deterministic - most consistent with a race between the relaunched client's local-replica read and its reconciliation of the expiry, which the harness catches because it checks with no tolerance window. It matters because the lane's own green bar (ENVIRONMENT.md) requires the choreography segment to pass for EVERY check, so on that attempt M5 would not have been green; it is minor rather than major because the brief's m5-a02 allows a tolerance for connected clients, no data is wrong, and the server correctly refuses the expired message throughout.

defects.summary: API.md never names the field carrying a failed mutation's refusal reason. It documents `denied` for queries and says 'A failed receipt or denied must be surfaced', but a failed mutation's reason lives in `why` ({code, family, message, rule, site}), which the document never mentions. A third-party client written from API.md alone can detect the failure but cannot surface its reason - which is what the same paragraph asks it to do. The diagnostics themselves are good; this is purely the documentation gap. The grader hit it directly: a first probe looked for a `failure` field and found null.

Above 60 by a clear margin: it is M1-M5 that are solid here, not M1-M4, and solid under independent grader re-execution (custom-client API, browser automation, source and store inspection) rather than only under the builder's suite - M1 13/13, M2 27/27, M3 15/15, M4 12/12, M5 12/12 - while M6 (6/13) and M8 (16/18) pass everything their gated web/API scope can demonstrate and both hold green receipts. Held below 90 by exactly the two things that anchor names: one in-scope milestone (M7, 0/9) has its entire checklist unpassed, and the platform-proof artifacts are absent for all nine native-artifact assertions (m6-a01..a07, m8-a17, m8-a18) - artifacts/m*-ios/ holds Expo/Hermes bundle exports, not the *-ios-screen.mp4 + *-ios-receipts.jsonl + *-ios-run.json triple simulator.md requires. O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path') and the 90 anchor ('only cosmetic nits'), nearer 90.
O2.justification: Zero blocker and zero major defects beyond the checklist; four minor and one cosmetic. Nothing found produces wrong user-visible data: all 58 independently re-executed suite-required assertions agreed with the suite (zero divergence), every trust boundary held (logged-out bearer 401; expired edit and delete refused server-side including a caller-supplied-timestamp variant; asset 404 after delete for both recipient and sender; view-once 410 on second and third fetch and 404 for a non-member; non-member searchChat NOT_MEMBER; non-member point query null; handle namespace input-validated so no case collision is possible), Trending's ranking matched read-only SQL ground truth exactly at 48270 in-window posts, digest counts were exact to the unit across five assertions including a mid-period backend restart with no double emission, and the invariant manifest conformed exactly. Short of 'only cosmetic nits' because three findings are more than nits: d-03 actually reddened the documented M6 entrypoint on a clean grader run, d-05 intermittently failed a frozen green-gate check (1 of 3 attempts), and d-01 defeats an explicit platform contract about presenting undecided results at the scale envelope. Evidence: grading/trace.md §5, §6.

O4.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush') and the 90 anchor ('reads, ordered queued writes, receipt transitions, and offline search all behave as specced on the native proof - on full runs including M8's durable-queue restart and multi-device convergence evidence'), just above 60.
O4.justification: Gate satisfied (M6 green). Admissible basis is the choreography receipts plus any simulator artifacts, and nothing else; simulator artifacts do not exist, so the basis is the harness's structured receipts, which the grader generated itself by running the byte-identical frozen harness. Demonstrated: offline writes show pending and flush IN ORDER (offline-message-queue-flush-in-order, flushMs 4662.2); receipt states walk normally after flush (same check plus m8-a16-dual-offline-receipts, totalMs 3541.4); warm-offline search over synced messages (1396 ms, both runs); M8 multi-device convergence with both clients offline settling in server-arrival order with no loss and no duplicates (m8-a15, firstFlushMs 2300.6 / secondFlushMs 2846.1). That is strictly better than the 60 anchor's broken-write picture. Not demonstrated by any admissible artifact: cold-start offline in its entirety (synced history, previously viewed media, cold-offline search, and the view-once photo NOT rendering - m6-a01..a04), pending state and ordered flush on the native carrier (m6-a05..a07), and M8's durable queue across app termination (m8-a17, m8-a18). Honesty of the gap, which this dimension scores explicitly, is exemplary and verified: README.md says 'these are Hermes exports, not simulator proofs' and run-record.json says 'simulator behavior is not claimed'; the grader inspected the artifacts and found exactly what the lane says they are, with no overclaim anywhere. Held short of 90 by the absent native proof rather than by any observed misbehaviour, with no dishonesty penalty. Evidence: grading/trace.md §4.6, §4.7, §4.9, §7.

O5.bandRationale: First-match over the order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. (0) does not fire: the invariant manifest CONFORMS - the lane's verification actual counts equal invariant-manifest-combined.json's expectedState.perEntityCounts field for field at the 10%, 50% and final states, the grader independently re-verified all five named O5 fixtures at the final state through the custom-client API before any probe ran (u0500 following 500 / conversations 100; u0005 following 5; celebrity u0900 followers 900 / posts 200; celebrity-follower u0901 following exactly u0001-u0004 plus u0900; busy group g0001 50 members and 10000 messages counted exactly by full paging over 500 complete pages), the committed scale.log hash matches its pin, and settledPrefix == actionCount == 167157 with failedActions 0; and the replay wall cap is a P3 placeholder in this frozen instrument, so there is no cap to exhaust. (30) does not fire: every evaluable degradation rule passes on grader-run k=20-after-3-warm-up sequential probes with a 30 s timeout - deep paging p95 16.48 ms vs the 42.66 ms 3x bound; following-feed 500-follow 8.83 ms vs 21.24 ms; celebrity read path 6.82 ms vs 21.24 ms; celebrity write path 70.66 ms vs 180.75 ms; receipt aggregation in the 50-member group 1.08x on send ack and 1.37x on history render versus a small chat; cold-start sync of the 100-conversation probe user completing in 599 ms at 119 MB RSS; global search 2.56x from the 10% checkpoint with the 50% sample on the line; and the Insights structural clause passing (840-byte payload, complete:true, meter examined 20, server-side aggregate views rather than paging the corpus to the client) - with zero timeouts, zero errors and zero OOMs across two full sweeps. (60) does not fire: absolute p95 ceilings are also P3 placeholders in this instrument version, and the replay cap is undefined, so neither 'any absolute ceiling is exceeded' nor 'replay used >80% of its cap' can fire. (90) does not fire: it is an affirmative condition over those same undefined ceilings and cap ('every probe's observed ceiling utilization <=50% AND replay used <=50% of its cap') and therefore cannot be established. (75) fires as the otherwise branch. Recorded limitation: the 10% and 50% checkpoint states no longer exist, so the three checkpoint-curve rules leaned on the lane's single-sample checkpoint probes - robust for global search (2.56x, far inside 3x) but unevaluable for Insights and Trending, for which no checkpoint baseline was ever recorded; their full-corpus p95s are ~5 ms with index-backed meters (Trending examined 62 rows over 48270 in-window posts), which is an absence of evidence of superlinear growth rather than a pass. Also recorded: run-record.json is the base protocol record and deliberately carries no performanceProbes.o5Inputs, so this band is derived from the replay receipts plus the grader's own measurements. Evidence: grading/trace.md §7 O5 block.

The consequence is that O3, whose applicability rule restricts it to 'the wave's secret rotated holdout probes only', has no admissible evidence and records null; its predicate (m6-green-and-m1-m5-attempted) is otherwise satisfied. Trust-boundary behaviour WAS exercised as part of the frozen checklist and as adjacent grader probes, and is published in grading/trace.md §5, but it feeds O1/O2 only and is deliberately not reported as a probe result. (2) This grader's family has not passed the calibration gate (grader/calibration.md), so calibrationPassed is false and the record labels the grade uncalibrated-grader; sameFamilyGraded is false (the builder harness is a Codex/gpt-6-astra session per run-record.json, a different family). (3) Timing-sensitive checks are judged best-of-3 with machine load recorded beside each record in grading/trace.md; this machine is shared and 1-minute load ranged from 3.99 to 62.10 during the session, which is the direct cause of the absorbed attempt failures noted in §4.9 and of defect d-05's intermittency. SCHEMA LIMITATION AND PRIOR MEASUREMENT-COVERAGE GAP: this frozen report schema constrains assertionResults keys to ^m[1-7]-a[0-9]{2}$ and therefore cannot hold M8 results, even though assertions.json and applicability.json both place M8 in the full-run scope and in O1/O2's observing set. To deliver a complete 119-assertion grade while staying schema-valid, the 101 M1-M7 ids are here and the 18 M8 ids are in grading/m8-assertion-results.json in the same record shape with the same enum values; no id appears in both files and together they partition the manifest's 119 ids exactly. The September 5 and September 12 structured assertionResults carried only those same 101 ids - their notes could describe M8 observations but they did not provide a machine-comparable 18-id M8 result set - so the prior-101 subtotal (85 pass / 0 fail / 16 not-run) is the only quantity directly comparable across the three dates, and the 18 M8 results (16 pass / 0 fail / 2 not-run) and the 119-result total are new measurement coverage rather than a change in lane behaviour. A separate manifest-internal inconsistency: assertions.json's own counts block says M2:24 and total:116 while the file carries 27 M2 assertions and 119 in total; grading followed the actual assertion objects, which is what the ids key against. Nothing is struck-by-environment in this run (ENVIRONMENT.md), so no assertion carries that status. No weighted total, efficiency statistic or cross-lane comparison is computed here - those are the harness's and publisher's jobs.
